text:
sqlpipe moves data from Postgres to S3 with three processes: a reader, a converter, and an uploader.

The reader streams rows from Postgres in batches. A batch is a fixed number of rows held in memory. Streaming keeps memory use low because the reader never loads the full table.

The converter turns each batch into a Parquet row group. Parquet is a columnar file format (data stored by column, not by row). A row group is one self-contained block of rows inside a Parquet file.

The uploader writes the Parquet data to S3 as multipart objects. A multipart upload sends a large object in separate parts. If a part fails, the uploader sends that part again. This retry logic makes the pipeline safe on unstable networks.
